_meta.business: A Singapore bubble tea chain — 3 outlets, soy-milk-based line, health positioning
_meta.form_fidelity: Form inputs are as a founder would supply them. The derived competitive set is included as EVIDENCE — this is the corrected pipeline (derive -> evidence -> score), not the old owner-list-only path.
_meta.no_label_written: No expected answer recorded. Compare against the delivered CaiCa analysis verdict.

form.category: Bubble tea — hand-shaken milk tea and fruit tea. 3 outlets, heartland and mall locations. A soy-milk-based line as a health positioning. Drinks largely at HPB Nutri-Grade B/C.
form.positioning_sentence: Singapore's first chain brewing tea with soy bean milk — a local, healthier bubble tea.
form.differentiator: We are the first chain in Singapore to brew with soy bean milk instead of dairy creamer. Local brand, founded here, and our drinks are healthier by Nutri-Grade measure than the standard milk tea. We also have a snack pairing line.
form.undercut_on: Price and visibility. The big chains have far more outlets and can promote harder. And the imported brands are opening everywhere.
form.their_price_point: There is cheap bubble tea under S$3.50. The mid-tier chains are around the same as us. Not sure about the premium ones.

customer_description: Students, office workers and families passing a mall or MRT station. Trigger is mostly impulse — walking past, or ordering delivery for home.

derived_competitive_set._note: EVIDENCE supplied by the derivation stage. This is what makes position_availability and competitive_room answerable — they were asked without this evidence in the Bonefirm and ObserveCo runs and came back at 0.19/0.38/0.45 confidence.

tier_0_default.why: Cheaper, no detour. Most drink occasions resolve here — bubble tea is a treat, not a habit.

members: Mixue (S$1.50-3.50, no membership, 30+ heartland and MRT outlets)
tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: Cheapest cup on the island. Mixue needs no app or membership and sits exactly where students and families pass.

members: KOI Thé (90 outlets: 62 cafés + 26 Express counters inside MRT stations and hospitals)
tier_2_direct_set.why: Same product, same occasion, already nearby. KOI's advantage is reach, not novelty. 62+ bubble tea brands operate in Singapore; 953 bubble tea businesses islandwide. No dominant player.

members: KOI Thé — 'Singaporeans' favourite by polling', the brand credited with starting the modern wave
CHAGEE — 'not a bubble tea brand, a tea expert'; original leaf tea, no powder, no creamer
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: The buyer is shopping for a TREAT DRINK, not for 'bubble tea'. The brand at the top of their mental list wins. KOI holds reach, CHAGEE holds the premium craft ladder, LiHO holds homegrown.
tier_3_category_incumbent.diagnostic: The owner named no member of this tier. The owner's claim is 'local + healthier'. CHAGEE grew fastest by REJECTING the bubble tea label the owner is embracing.

members: convenience-store RTD tea (CHAGEE teabags now on FairPrice shelves at S$12/8 = ~S$1.90 a home cup)
tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: Takes the same treat-drink occasion with a different product. A S$6.50 coffee and a S$6.50 milk tea are the same decision to a buyer wanting a nice cold drink.

tier_6_indirect.why: Not a purchase rival — dilutes the number of treat occasions.

_notes_for_harness.what_changed_from_the_old_pipeline: For the first time the scorer receives a DERIVED competitive set as evidence. Bonefirm and ObserveCo were scored against an owner-supplied list only, which is why position_availability and competitive_room came back at low confidence. This run tests whether supplied evidence resolves that.
_notes_for_harness.the_owner_named_almost_nothing: Two entries — 'KOI' and 'the imported Chinese brands'. That is the blindspot probe: it should be a large delta against the derived set.
_notes_for_harness.compare_against: The delivered CaiCa analysis. Its verdict: the local + healthier wedge is shared, copyable and contradicted by the actual taste; CHAGEE is the dominant frame; the product must be fixed before any position is worth taking.
